analyst_view.overall: Early view: a relegation six-pointer between 17th-placed Rio Ave (7 points, 24 conceded) and 16th-placed Casa Pia (8 points, only 6 scored). Vasco Seabra has his president's backing but is under pressure after a 4-0 home defeat by Famalicão; centre-back Ntoi's two-match ban from 5 November should be served by now, and Brandon Aguilera is back in training after a long knee injury. My research on Casa Pia's own team news is thin.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Rio Ave's defence leaks (24 in 11), but Casa Pia have the league's weakest attack (6 in 11), and relegation six-pointers often get tense. Those factors cancel out around the site's figure.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, which looks high. Casa Pia's attack rarely puts teams under sustained pressure, so their expected 4.8 corners seems generous. I lean lower.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. I lean higher: it is a bottom-of-the-table game, and Rio Ave's last trip to Viseu ended in a brawl with Ntoi and Petrasso both punished. Both sides need points badly.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.3 shots. Casa Pia create very little and Rio Ave's attack has 9 goals in 11 games. I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. With two of the league's three weakest attacks, I expect fewer efforts on target. The return of Aguilera could help Rio Ave, but after nine months out he is unlikely to start.
